bug_description.original: Use-of-uninitialized-value in vcardtime_from_string OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=505903588 ``` Crash type: Use-of-uninitialized-value Crash state: vcardtime_from_string vcardvalue_new_from_string _parse_vcard ```
bug_description.normalized: The vCard parser forwards an attacker-controlled property value into the date/time parser. In `sscanf_time()`, the `ndig == 2` and `str[2] == ':'` branch inspects `str[8]` to decide whether to parse fractional seconds, but it does not first prove that the string has at least nine bytes. A short colon-form time string therefore makes the parser read past the initialized end of the fuzz input buffer, and MemorySanitizer reports that read as a use of uninitialized value.

source.description: The parser materializes the attacker-controlled property value text from `state->buf` and passes it into typed value parsing.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness copies attacker-controlled `data,size` into a NUL-terminated string and `vcardparser_parse_string()` accumulates the current property's bytes in `state->buf` before this call.
source.note: After reading a property's value bytes, `_parse_prop_value()` turns the accumulated input into `buf_cstring(&state->buf)` and hands that exact string to `vcardvalue_new_from_string()`. This is the first project statement that creates the vulnerability-relevant time-like string from attacker input.

relation.description: The parser-produced property value string is passed into typed value construction.

root_cause.description: The time parser reads the ninth byte of the string to test for fractional seconds without first checking that the colon-form input is long enough to have an index 8.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `strlen(str) > 8 &&` before this condition. In the vulnerable code, reaching the `ndig == 2` and `str[2] == ':'` branch is enough to evaluate `str[8]` even when the attacker-controlled string is shorter than nine initialized bytes.

sink.description: The unsafe indexed read consumes the short attacker-controlled time string and triggers the MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value report.
sink.note: MSan reports the crash at `sscanf_time` line 456:21 on the `str[8]` read. This is the concrete out-of-bounds/poisoned byte consumption that the missing length guard permits.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz harness copies attacker-controlled bytes into `vcard_string` before project parsing. This is provenance only; scored anchors stay in project code.

parser_admitted.description: The input reaches the accepted property-parsing continuation once the parser recognizes a property name and allocates `state->prop` for it; malformed names would return `PE_NAME_INVALID` instead of continuing to value parsing.

fine_trace.note: After the property value bytes have been accumulated, the parser materializes them as `buf_cstring(&state->buf)` and passes that attacker-controlled string into typed value parsing.
When `state->value_kind` is one of the time-capable kinds, the same attacker-controlled string is dispatched into `vcardtime_from_string(str, kind == VCARD_TIME_VALUE)` for date/time parsing.

depends_on.via: state->value_kind == VCARD_DATE_VALUE || state->value_kind == VCARD_TIME_VALUE || state->value_kind == VCARD_DATETIME_VALUE || state->value_kind == VCARD_DATEANDORTIME_VALUE || state->value_kind == VCARD_TIMESTAMP_VALUE

fine_trace.note: For a non-empty remainder, `vcardtime_from_string()` optionally skips a leading `T` and forwards the resulting substring to `sscanf_time()` without adding any minimum-length check for the later `str[8]` access.

On the branch where the string begins with two digits and a colon, the parser immediately inspects `str[8]` to choose the fractional-seconds format. There is no guard proving `strlen(str) > 8` before this indexed read.

When the attacker-controlled substring is shorter than nine initialized bytes, evaluating `str[8]` reads past the initialized end of the fuzz input string. MemorySanitizer reports this exact read at line 456:21 as the use of uninitialized value.

poc.trigger: The saved witness is a 268-byte vCard-like text input that drives `_parse_vcard()` into property-value parsing and then into `vcardtime_from_string()`. The staged fix and MSan trace support only the narrow claim that the attacker-controlled value reaching `sscanf_time()` is short enough that the vulnerable `if (str[8] == '.')` test reads beyond the initialized end of that substring.

format.name: vCard text parsed by libicalvcard_fuzzer
format.contract: A NUL-terminated text input accepted far enough by `vcardparser_parse_string()` to reach `_parse_prop_value()` with a property whose `state->value_kind` dispatches to the date/time parser, where the value substring passed to `sscanf_time()` satisfies `ndig == 2` and `str[2] == ':'` but is not proven to have more than eight initialized bytes. The saved artifacts do not justify a broader claim about all short time strings or a specific property name.
